open_items.exit_criteria: Qualify the v0.29.1-v0.29.5 release fixes outside the 104 policy/wire differential scenarios, including map-stream peer removal/rekey and SSH revocation/replay, OIDC callback safety, node lifecycle, DNS, and database upgrade/drop-in behavior, with paired process or stock-client evidence.
open_items.observed_blocker: Fresh and imported SQLite files use the pinned Go primary schema, and existing Rust-managed or supported older Go files auto-convert on first startup after a recoverable backup. A TLS stock-client handoff now proves a live Go v0.28.0 → Rust → Go v0.29.5 switch for two nodes and an approved route. Wider historical upgrade states and broader release qualification remain open.

A guarded export remains available for legacy Rust databases and rejects populated Rust-only tables. The Postgres row directly restarts pinned Go on the Rust-mutated database and reads the same selected users, nodes, keys, and route. A fresh production Rust SQLite database directly restarts pinned Go with user and key rows; its primary file has the pinned Go tables and a separate persistent Rust sidecar. A guarded offline converter preserved all five Go tables, six populated Rust-only tables, and SQLite sequences from a fully migrated legacy beta.2 snapshot; production Rust and pinned Go both reopened the output. A production Rust startup automatically converted a seeded beta.2 file in place after a backup, preserved all six populated auxiliary tables and ID sequences, and passed direct pinned-Go restart. The process row preserves a Rust-created user, preauth/API keys, one registered node, its approved subnet route, and the same Noise public key across both switches. The SQLite SQLx path retains its beta.2 intermediate stamp until file-backed conversion completes. A paired pinned-Go v0.29.5/Rust production Postgres stock-client lifecycle row now checks live map-stream peer visibility before and after restart: the observer initially sees two peers, then retains the expired peer as offline while the deleted peer disappears.
